Issue #163: a PEM body whose line breaks are literal two-character \n JSON-string escapes (as raw file bytes, not real newline bytes) rather than real newline bytes -- the shape a JSON-escaped export produces before any JSON-string unescaping -- is still detected. The 16-byte base64-run threshold in has_encoded_body is dwarfed by any realistic key-body line length, so the literal backslash breaking the run at each escape does not create a false negative; verified, no detector change needed.

Issue #163: a synthetic GCP/Firebase service-account key export -- the private_key field's PEM body carries JSON-escaped \n line breaks, with type/private_key_id/client_email present as surrounding context. The structural PEM match alone finds the key; the service-account shape is not consulted (per the issue's acceptance criteria, it is optional corroborating evidence only, never a substitute for the structural match). False-negative risk: a body deliberately re-wrapped at under 16 bytes per escaped line could still evade the run-length check; that pathological shape does not occur in real key exports and is not covered here.
